articles.title: Cantinho gamer: quanto custa montar um do zero na Black Friday? | G1
articles.standfirst: Com PC ou notebook potente, monitor rápido e cadeira confortável, 'kit básico' para jogar sem travar parte de R$ 5,9 mil; confira dicas para economizar.
articles.summary: Aprenda a montar seu cantinho gamer com investimento inicial de R$ 5,9 mil, priorizando componentes como a RTX 3060 e cadeiras ergonômicas para economizar na Black Friday.
articles.body:
Seja para mergulhar no mundo dos jogos ou para trabalhar com programas pesados de edição e design, montar um setup gamer exige planejamento.

A variedade de peças e acessórios no mercado é enorme e, com a alta de preços causada pela crise dos chips de memória RAM , a conta pode sair do controle muito rápido.

Por isso, a chegada da Black Friday no fim de novembro vira a oportunidade perfeita para quem quer economizar e garantir componentes melhores pagando menos.

Para ajudar quem não quer gastar mais do que o necessário, o Guia de Compras calculou o investimento inicial para montar uma estrutura completa, da máquina aos periféricos.

No total, um setup equilibrado custa entre R$ 5.900 e R$ 10.300 (preços consultados em novembro). Veja abaixo o que você precisa priorizar e quanto vai gastar em cada item.

O coração do setup é a máquina. Na hora de escolher, o usuário tem dois caminhos: a praticidade e mobilidade de um notebook gamer ou a possibilidade de upgrades futuros de um desktop (PC já montado).

Para conseguir rodar a maioria dos lançamentos mais recentes sem engasgos, a recomendação é buscar configurações que atendam a um padrão mínimo de desempenho:

Processador: Intel Core i5, AMD Ryzen 5 ou acima;

Placa de vídeo: GeForce RTX 3060 ou superior.

Dependendo dos componentes escolhidos, um PC ou notebook pode custar de R$ 5.000 a R$ 8.000.

Especificações: Intel Core I5 10ª geração, 16GB RAM, RTX 3060, SSD 1TB

Especificações: AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS, 8GB RAM, RTX 4050, SSD 512GB

Se a sua escolha for um computador de mesa, a tela é obrigatória. Mas, mesmo para quem optou pelo notebook, ter um segundo monitor na mesa faz toda a diferença para a experiência visual.

No universo dos jogos, mais importante do que a resolução é a taxa de atualização (medida em Hertz), que garante imagens mais fluidas e sem rastros em cenas rápidas de ação.

Para isso, o ideal é optar por telas com taxas entre 100 Hz e 144 Hz, que custam desde R$ 600 até R$ 1.000.

Especificações: 23.8", Full HD, 144Hz, LED IPS

Especificações: 23.8", Full Hd, 240Hz, Fast IPS

O visual das cadeiras estilizadas do tipo "gamer" costuma chamar atenção, mas muitos modelos de entrada priorizam as cores e o formato de banco de corrida em vez do suporte à coluna, além de esquentarem com facilidade.

Por isso, a dica de ouro para cuidar da saúde é apostar nas cadeiras ergonômicas de escritório, de preferência com encosto em tela respirável (mesh), apoio lombar e regulagem de altura nos braços.

Dá para encontrar modelos mais simples a partir de R$ 300, enquanto os mais equipados podem chegar a R$ 1.000.

Para fechar o pacote, os periféricos garantem o controle das ações. Se a ideia for economizar ao máximo no início, é possível encontrar combos básicos de teclado de membrana e mouse óptico a partir de R$ 80.

Porém, para quem busca durabilidade e precisão competitiva, vale investir um pouco mais em um teclado mecânico (com respostas mais rápidas e teclas individuais) e em um mouse gamer com sensor preciso e ajuste de DPI.

Nesse caso, o preço do conjunto sobe para cerca de R$ 300.

Com a configuração mais simples, o consumidor vai precisar desembolsar cerca de R$ 5.900.

Já quem quer uma máquina com margem para rodar jogos nas qualidades gráficas máximas, aliada a periféricos mecânicos e uma cadeira ergonômica com mais ajustes, vai precisar reservar mais de R$ 10.000.

A dica para quem está com o orçamento curto é começar pelo essencial (a máquina e a cadeira) e deixar os periféricos mais avançados para compras futuras.

articles.title: Decoração de Natal: 6 dicas para evitar acidentes e economizar | G1
articles.standfirst: A revisão das instalações internas do imóvel e a escolha dos itens que vão fazer parte da decoração são cruciais para prevenir acidentes e economizar na conta.
articles.summary: Decoração de Natal: especialista orienta sobre o uso de LEDs e revisões elétricas para prevenir incêndios e garantir economia na conta de luz deste mês.
articles.body:
A proximidade da data que celebra o Natal, comemorado em 25 de dezembro, motiva a decoração de casas e empreendimentos, principalmente com luzes coloridas. À Rede Clube, o engenheiro Abraão Galeno listou 6 dicas de segurança e prevenção de acidentes das instalações elétricas natalinas.

O especialista, que também é executivo de Estudos e Desempenho do Sistema da Equatorial Piauí, ressaltou que cuidados como a revisão das instalações internas do imóvel e escolha dos itens que vão fazer parte da decoração são essenciais para a prevenção de acidentes.

"É importante a gente prestar atenção em alguns fatores, como no momento da compra do pisca-pisca ou da reutilização desse produto. [...] É importante verificar a extensão do produto, se não tem indícios de remendos, de desgaste natural, e nunca usar as extensões, porque a utilização do "T" sobrecarrega aquele ponto de energia", destaca Abraão.

O engenheiro recomenda ainda que o equipamento chamado filtro de linha é uma opção para quem deseja utilizar várias tomadas ao mesmo tempo.

Abraão também orienta que se evite a instalação de iluminação próxima a cortinas e papéis, que podem ser inflamados.

"Em caso de choque elétrico, que a gente não quer que aconteça, é importante desligar o disjuntor e retirar a pessoa com segurança, utilizando material isolante como madeira, daquele ambiente", finalizou o executivo.

Entre as medidas para economizar na conta de luz, a Equatorial orienta que utilizar pisca-pisca com lâmpadas de LED, estabelecer um horário para ligar e desligar os enfeites, além de não usar produtos com fios desencapados podem diminuir o consumo nesse período . Ignorar essas ações podem provocar choques, curtos-circuitos e incêndios, além de aumentar o consumo de energia.

Veja recomendações para uma instalação mais segura:

Monte a árvore de natal distante de cortinas ou quaisquer outros objetos/materiais que possam propagar chamas em caso de curto curto-circuito;

Sempre que for se ausentar de casa, retire os itens decorativos da tomada;

Fique atento com a ornamentação de áreas externas, por conta das chuvas e fortes ventos que ocorrem neste período, o que agrava os riscos de acidentes, como choques, curtos-circuitos e até incêndios, além do perigo de quedas;

Não decore lugares próximos à rede elétrica, para evitar que encostem nos cabos de tensão;

Não use os postes da rede elétrica para ornamentação ou para servir de apoio;

Deve-se evitar o contato das lâmpadas com objetos e enfeites que podem ser inflamáveis, como cortinas e tapetes.

Em caso de acidente ou emergência com a rede elétrica, isole a área e ligue imediatamente para:

articles.title: Motorista é resgatado de capotamento com ajuda de poste de madeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu em uma estrada vicinal próxima à BR-365, na tarde deste domingo (22). A vítima sofreu traumas na região pélvica e abdominal e foi levada ao Hospital de Clínicas da UFU.
articles.summary: Após acidente em Uberlândia, motorista com traumas pélvicos e abdominais foi socorrido com ajuda de populares e levado ao Hospital de Clínicas da UFU neste domingo.
articles.body:
Populares improvisaram um poste madeira para ajudar motorista sair de carro após capotamento em Uberlândia — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Reprodução

Um motorista, de idade não divulgada, ficou ferido após perder o controle do veículo e capotar em uma via vicinal próxima à BR-365, ao lado do Posto Laranjeiras, em Uberlândia , na tarde deste domingo (22).

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado com a informação de que havia uma vítima presa às ferragens. Quando as equipes chegaram ao local, encontraram o veículo capotado fora da pista e com uma estabilização provisória utilizando um poste de madeira feita por populares, que conseguiram retirar o motorista do interior do carro .

Os bombeiros realizaram os primeiros atendimentos até a chegada de uma equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu). Segundo a corporação, o motorista apresentava traumas nas regiões pélvica e abdominal.

Após os procedimentos iniciais, a vítima foi encaminhada pelo Samu para o Pronto-Socorro do Hospital de Clínicas da Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (HC-UFU).

Ainda conforme os bombeiros, depois do resgate foram realizados o desligamento da bateria do veículo e a retirada do automóvel da via para garantir a segurança e liberar o acesso de veículos que transitavam por um setor de chácaras da região.

O carro ficou sob responsabilidade de amigos da vítima. As circunstâncias que levaram ao capotamento não foram informadas .

articles.title: Two Carneys, a fake Donald Trump: Canada PM turns press gallery dinner into a roast
articles.summary: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney brought out a Donald Trump impersonator during a press event.
articles.body: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney brought out a Donald Trump impersonator during a press event. The impersonator went on to mock the US president’s trade negotiations, his repeated suggestion that Canada become the 51st state and even his search for a new press secretary.The Saturday night roast at the Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner in Ottawa featured two Carneys and a Trump, as comedians Mark McKinney and Mark Critch impersonated the Canadian prime minister and the US president. The event, Canada’s version of Washington’s political roast, also saw opposition leaders and senior officials take aim at Carney, former prime minister Justin Trudeau and each other.Critch, playing Trump, stormed onto the stage with the president’s trademark hand gestures, dance moves and aggressive handshake, pulling Carney away from the lectern before launching into a parody of US-Canada trade negotiations.“Mark, we’re going to have an incredible deal. I call him Mark, I don’t call him ‘the governor’ to his face because I’m a coward,” the impersonator said, mocking Trump’s repeated suggestion that Canada should become the 51st US state.“But we’re gonna have a great deal. There’s only one thing standing in the way: me, because I’m crazy,” he added, as the audience erupted in laughter.The fake Trump also poked fun at Carney’s popularity, saying: “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster. Isn’t this incredible. Two Carneys, he’s so popular. Almost as popular as me.”In a particularly irreverent moment, the impersonator compared the two leaders to the gay hockey romance Heated Rivalry, joking: “It’s like Heated Rivalry if the hockey players were straight and all goalies.”He then turned to Carney and added: “But he’s got a great a**, doesn’t he? What a beautiful a**.”The skit also took aim at Trump’s search for a new press secretary after a brief stint by Katie Zacharia. The impersonator said he was at the dinner because he needed a press secretary and was looking for a “beautiful” one, while dismissing candidates who were “too smart”.The fake Trump also joked about finding an ambassador “less likable than me” and delivered the line: “He puts the a** in ambassador.”Carney takes aim at Trump’s Oval Office makeoverCarney had his own shots ready for Trump, mocking the US president’s lavish makeover of the Oval Office, which has been filled with gold accents, gilded decorations and portraits.“This is a tough room. And I’ve been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its new interior decorator,” Carney said.The Canadian prime minister also poked fun at his own speech from the previous week, when he was asked about Quebecor’s proposal to acquire Telus. Carney had suggested that, under certain circumstances, an oligopoly could lead to more competition.“My staff are going to hate me for this, but this reminds me of a good oligopoly joke that I heard the other day. All the telcos told it to me at the same time,” he said.“Look, there are market structures in which that actually would be funny.”Carney ended his speech by joking that his office’s readout of the evening would record that he was “both absolutely hilarious and largely statesmanlike”.“Largely’ is maybe doing a lot of work in that sentence,” he added.Poilievre, Trudeau and the ‘faded pop princess’Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre also took aim at Carney, joking about reports that the prime minister has a controlling leadership style, micromanages staff and is harsh with journalists.“Some say that Mark has a controlling leadership style. There’s been reports that he yells and micromanages his staff. He acts like a miserable prick to journalists. And when I hear things like that, I say once again, he’s stealing all my ideas,” Poilievre said.He also mocked former prime minister Trudeau’s relationship with American pop star Katy Perry, saying Trudeau was doing to a “faded pop princess” what he had done to Canada during his decade in power. The remark drew criticism online for being sexist and demeaning towards Perry.Poilievre ended his speech with a dig at government funding for journalism, carrying a bag of money onto the stage and pretending to hand out cash to media organisations.Governor General Louise Arbour, who represents King Charles III as Canada’s head of state, also took a swipe at the prime minister’s extensive international travel.“Do you know the difference between God and Mark Carney? God is everywhere, and Mark Carney is everywhere except in Ottawa, where he’s supposed to be,” she said.The dinner ended with the usual political barbs, but the evening’s biggest laughs came from the unlikely sight of two Carneys sharing a stage with a fake Trump, turning the strained Canada-US relationship into the night’s central punchline.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Canadian homeowner sued after a buyer failed to complete an C$18 million home purchase and the property later sold at a loss; an appeals court reversed a ruling that had set aside a C$4.26 million damages order
articles.summary: A Canadian judge has given a buyer another chance to defend himself in a dispute over an C$18 million property deal that fell through in 2021.
articles.body: A Canadian judge has given a buyer another chance to defend himself in a dispute over an C$18 million property deal that fell through in 2021. The decision cancels a C$4.26 million order against Stephen Brown, who had agreed to buy the property from Rakesh Dhunna but did not complete the purchase.Dhunna later sold the property for C$14.3 million, which was C$3.7 million less than the agreed price. He took Brown to court and secured an order for C$4,262,369.40 in compensation after the buyer failed to respond to the case.Brown eventually approached the court to challenge the order. He argued that he had reasons to defend himself and also questioned how the seller's losses had been calculated.In a decision dated March 25, Justice Stephens of the British Columbia Supreme Court allowed Brown to contest the claim. The judge cancelled the earlier orders and gave him 30 days to file his response.Property sold for C$14.3 millionAccording to the informationa available in the judgment, Brown and Dhunna signed the purchase agreement on April 17, 2021. The agreed price was C$18 million, but the sale did not go through.Dhunna filed a case against Brown on September 16. Brown received the legal notice five days later but did not respond within the required 21 days.As a result, Dhunna obtained a court order in November in his favour. The property was eventually sold in April 2023 for C$14.3 million.Dhunna then sought compensation for the difference between the original sale price and the amount received from the later sale. He also included expenses incurred while holding the property. On July 18, 2023, the court ordered Brown to pay C$4,262,369.40.Buyer disputes seller's lossesWhen Brown challenged the order, he questioned why Dhunna had not accepted an earlier offer for the property. He told the court that the seller had received an offer of C$14.8 million in February 2022 but did not accept it. The property was sold for C$14.3 million in April 2023.Brown argued that accepting the earlier offer would have reduced the amount claimed against him by C$500,000. He also questioned the expenses of about C$562,369 that Dhunna had included for keeping the property until it was sold.Buyer explains why he did not respondBrown did not ask the court to cancel the earlier order until June 30, 2025, more than three years after it was issued. He had represented himself in the case until April 2025, when he hired a lawyer.He told the court that he had not understood the legal process or realised that he could ask for the earlier decision to be reconsidered. He believed the property deal was no longer active and said he was also dealing with personal and financial difficulties.Brown's affidavit mentioned the deaths of his father in Saskatchewan and his wife's niece in Oregon during this period.The judge found that Brown had not deliberately ignored the original case. However, the court also noted that he had waited a long time before taking steps to challenge the order. His personal circumstances did not fully explain why he had allowed so much time to pass.Dispute over purchase conditionsBrown also raised questions about the conditions attached to the original property agreement. Dhunna relied on an addendum dated April 23, 2021, which he said showed that Brown had agreed to remove certain conditions from the deal.Brown acknowledged that the signature on the document appeared to be his but said he did not remember signing it. He denied agreeing to remove the conditions. The judge also noted that Dhunna's signature was missing from the document, although there was a space for it.The court did not decide whether the conditions had been removed. However, the judge found that the disagreement needed to be examined further because it could affect whether Brown was required to complete the purchase.You use AI every day. articles.title: A British couple bought a 72-foot World War II boat on eBay for £6,500 and spent years restoring it; the vessel once helped guide Allied troops towards Gold Beach during D-Day
articles.summary: A British couple bought a 72-foot World War II boat on eBay for £6,500 to save it from being scrapped, unaware that their restoration project would
articles.body: A British couple bought a 72-foot World War II boat on eBay for £6,500 to save it from being scrapped, unaware that their restoration project would attract thousands of supporters. Simon and Gemma Robins purchased the former harbour defence vessel, known as L1392 during its military service, in January 2021. The boat once served as a navigation leader during Operation Neptune, helping guide Allied troops towards Gold Beach during the D-Day invasion. After years of changing roles, including becoming a luxury motor yacht, the 59-tonne vessel was decommissioned in 2013. The couple now hope to turn it into a holiday home.How a £6,500 WWII boat bought on eBay guided Allied troops on D-DayThe boat served as a navigation leader during Operation Neptune, the seaborne invasion of northern France known as D-Day. According to Marine Industry News, it was part of the ML Flotilla and helped guide Allied troops towards Gold Beach during the pivotal invasion.More than 400 Harbour Defence Launches (HDMLs) were constructed around 80 years ago, but very few remain today. L1392's wartime service was followed by several changes in its role and identity, with the vessel continuing to operate after the war before undergoing further transformations.How the WWII boat transformed from a military vessel into a luxury yachtAfter the war, the vessel was repurposed as a fast dispatch boat before being transferred to the UK's customs agency. By the 1970s, it had been transformed into a charter vessel and renamed Sarinda. It subsequently underwent several reinventions, including conversion into a luxury motor yacht, before being decommissioned in 2013.The Robins bought the 59-tonne vessel knowing that repairing it would involve substantial costs and a great deal of work. They did not intend to restore it to its original military appearance, instead hoping to use it as a holiday home one day. However, the couple said they had not made definite plans for its long-term future.YouTube channel attracting thousands to a £6,500 WWII boat restorationGemma launched the YouTube channel Ship Happens to share restoration updates with family members. The channel went on to attract viewers worldwide, with Marine Industry News reporting that it had approximately 26,000 subscribers in May 2021, along with thousands of people watching its episodes.The success of the channel also led the couple to sell merchandise, while subscribers contributed donations towards the restoration costs and sent gifts to the family. Gemma told Marine Industry News: “We said [it would take] 10 years when we first bought it, but YouTube is accelerating the project.” She added that the growing interest and contributions were helping them move the work forward, despite their existing bills and commitments.You use AI every day. articles.body: AGRA: A tourist from Delhi on Sunday alleged that he and his family members were assaulted by CISF personnel at the Taj Mahal’s eastern gate following a dispute over the identity documents of his three-year-old son.A Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) official, however, denied the allegation, saying an altercation took place between the personnel and the tourist over the use of the VIP gate, news agency PTI reported.The tourist, Sajid, said his son had gone missing inside the monument for around five minutes before being found with a CISF official. The personnel allegedly asked him to produce the child’s Aadhaar card.Sajid said he showed photographs of himself and the child on his mobile phone, along with the child’s birth certificate, to establish that the boy was his son.Despite this, the personnel insisted on an Aadhaar card and allegedly told Sajid that he would get his child back only after four days if he failed to produce the document, PTI reported.He further alleged that the CISF personnel snatched his mobile phone and severely assaulted his brother-in-law, Azad. The latter subsequently lost consciousness and was taken to hospital.Superintending Archaeologist Dr Smita S Kumar said she had received information about the altercation between the tourists and CISF personnel.“We have sought a report from our officials in this regard. An explanation will also be sought from the CISF commandant. articles.title: Microsoft is changing how it pays employees in its cloud unit; memo from Azure boss Arun Ulagaratchagan says: Pay-for-performance only works if we are...
articles.summary: Microsoft is tying pay in its Azure cloud division more closely to performance, a month after it offered tens of thousands of employees a way out.
articles.body: Microsoft is tying pay in its Azure cloud division more closely to performance, a month after it offered tens of thousands of employees a way out. Top performers in Azure will get additional stock awards, while those with weaker results will face formal meetings with their managers. The change was set out in an internal memo from Arun Ulagaratchagan, executive vice president of Azure, which Bloomberg reviewed. Taken together with October's buyout offer to 60,000 employees, it shows how Microsoft is reshaping its workforce while it spends heavily on AI."Pay-for-performance only works if we are equally rigorous on both sides: recognizing exceptional impact and being honest when performance falls short," Ulagaratchagan wrote in the memo.He also raised the bar for everyone else. "Meeting today's bar means closing previous performance gaps and demonstrating a meaningful step-change in impact," he wrote. He added that AI is reshaping how the world works and that competition has never been more intense.Microsoft has confirmed the update, which went out to Azure staff on Thursday. "A world-class team like Azure requires world-class talent," a company spokesperson told Bloomberg. The spokesperson said the new model includes "meaningful additional awards" for the strongest performers, along with clear expectations and timely, direct feedback from managers.Microsoft's Azure pay change follows its 60,000-employee buyout offerThe memo builds on a move Microsoft made last month. On October 26, the company offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its 223,000-strong workforce. Eligible staff in India at level 70 and below were included. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said the offer gave employees "who may be considering a future outside the company" a chance to make that move now, with support.The buyout was aimed at employees thinking of leaving. The pay model is aimed at the ones who stay, with bigger rewards at the top and closer scrutiny at the bottom. Even before the memo, a pay spreadsheet put together by employees reportedly showed the largest stock awards already going to cloud and AI workers.Satya Nadella links the buyouts and pay to how AI is changing jobsCEO Satya Nadella has described both moves as part of the same shift. Speaking at the DealBook Summit last week, he said the buyouts were offered "to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices."He said every Microsoft employee will eventually work as a manager of AI agents. As an example he gave the team behind Cowork, the agent in Microsoft 365 apps, which he said has just 11 developers. "They build a software factory that builds the product," he said. The harder part is getting a 51-year-old company to work that way. "So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?" Nadella said. He added that some people may decide they have "other choices" they want to make.Azure's pay overhaul comes amid reports of a 20% cost-cutting pushPaying top performers more also takes money. In October, The Information reported that Girish Bablani, who runs the Azure group that builds software for Microsoft's cloud servers, had asked team leaders to find ways to cut costs by at least 20%. According to the report, the savings would help pay for AI data centres and fund higher pay for engineers being courted by Meta and Anthropic. Microsoft disputed the report and said Azure leadership "has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans."The Information also reported that cloud chief Scott Guthrie was reshaping Azure's leadership, putting Ulagaratchagan in charge of Bablani, Azure CTO Mark Russinovich and security head Charlie Bell.Microsoft has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditure for calendar 2026. Azure is still its fastest-growing business, with sales up 48% last quarter.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Farmers planted trees across Tasmania’s cleared farmland to restore nature, but a study of 56 plantations found that even 20-year-old sites had only 33% to 43% of natural forest habitat scores
articles.summary: Planting trees on farmland can help restore habitats, but it does not necessarily bring back the biodiversity found in natural forests.
articles.body: Planting trees on farmland can help restore habitats, but it does not necessarily bring back the biodiversity found in natural forests. Researchers assessed 56 woody plantings across agricultural landscapes in Tasmania, examining how their age and composition affected habitat features and native plant life. The study, published in Restoration Ecology, found that even plantings around 20 years old had average habitat scores of only 33% to 43% of those recorded in natural reference forests. Native plant recovery was also limited, with researchers finding little evidence that many species had returned naturally.Tree planting on farms in Tasmania did not fully restore natural forest biodiversityThe research, titled 'Quantifying biodiversity benefits of woody plantings on Tasmanian farms for natural capital accounting,' examined agroforestry and revegetation projects in Tasmania's Midlands region. The area has experienced extensive land clearing since European colonisation began in the 1820s, with more than 80% of its native grasslands, grassy eucalypt woodlands and eucalypt forests cleared.Researchers Suzanne M. Prober, Georg Wiehl, Gary Ogden, Sue Ogilvy and Felipe E. Albornoz assessed 56 tree plantings alongside 12 remnant eucalypt forests and 12 improved pastures. The plantings ranged from 1.5 to 30 years old and included native mixed plantings, native monocultures and exotic monocultures. The team compared their habitat characteristics and plant diversity with those of natural reference forests to estimate the gains associated with restoration.The results showed that tree planting improved several habitat features over time, including tree cover and the development of larger trees. Yet the benefits remained well below natural forest reference levels. The researchers found that average habitat scores in 20-year-old plantings reached only 0.33 to 0.43 of reference values, depending on the planting type and assessment.Tasmanian native plants struggled to return to restored agricultural landscapesThe study found a more limited recovery when researchers looked specifically at native plant biodiversity. Native plant cover and species richness in native plantings reached up to 35% of reference values, but much of this reflected the species originally introduced during planting. The researchers detected no clear benefits for native ground-layer plants, while exotic plantings showed no measurable gains in native plant biodiversity.Plantings also did not become increasingly similar to natural forests simply as they grew older. The researchers found no consistent increase in native plant richness, cover or species composition with planting age. This suggests that establishing trees alone may not be enough to encourage a wider range of native plants to recolonise agricultural land.The authors also found that the choice of biodiversity measure affected how successful a planting appeared. Estimates based on similarity between native plant communities and natural reference forests were less than half those based on plant species richness or cover. In other words, counting the number of species or measuring their coverage could give a more favourable impression than examining whether the plant community resembled a natural forest.Researchers say understorey restoration is needed to improve biodiversity gainsAccording to the researchers' findings, woody plantings can provide habitat features with the potential to support fauna, but those improvements should not be mistaken for a full recovery of native biodiversity. Habitat scores increased substantially during the first 20 years, then continued to rise more slowly. The authors noted that some features, including large trees and logs, can take much longer to develop, with woody habitat recovery potentially extending beyond 100 years.The study suggests that additional restoration work beneath the tree canopy could make a difference. Native understorey plants, including grasses, herbs and shrubs, were not returning readily to the plantings. The researchers pointed to the need for further interventions to strengthen these parts of the ecosystem rather than relying on planted trees to trigger recovery on their own.The findings also have implications for natural capital accounting, which attempts to measure changes in the value of ecosystems and the benefits delivered by restoration projects. The authors argue that assessments need to consider which biodiversity measures are being used, since different metrics can produce very different estimates of restoration success. Their work provides a framework for measuring those gains on farms, while showing that more trees do not automatically mean a return to natural forest biodiversity.You use AI every day. articles.title: US Army to detonate 5 tons of explosives in Iowa: The reason and the controversy
articles.summary: The US Army has rescheduled the controlled detonation of nearly five tons of unstable lead azide at a military ammunition plant in Iowa to Wednesday,
articles.body: The US Army has rescheduled the controlled detonation of nearly five tons of unstable lead azide at a military ammunition plant in Iowa to Wednesday, citing weather conditions and safety measures. The decision comes as environmental groups challenge the operation in court and the Army seeks to invoke emergency provisions to proceed without an environmental permit.In a post on X on Sunday, the Army said the detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown had been moved to Wednesday “to allow for optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced”.“The Army and our interagency partners have been working around the clock to safeguard all Americans in the region,” the statement said. “The health and safety of all Americans has and always will be our first priority.”The operation was initially scheduled for Friday but has been postponed multiple times amid public concern and legal proceedings. The Army had earlier announced on Thursday that it would move the detonation to Monday, November 23.Why does the Army want to detonate the chemicals?The material involved is lead azide, an explosive chemical used in the manufacture of munitions. Army personnel discovered several dozen barrels of degraded lead azide at the facility in March. According to officials, crystallisation had made the material unstable and increased the risk of an accidental explosion.The Army has argued that handling the barrels or attempting to neutralise their contents could trigger a fatal detonation. Officials have also warned that falling temperatures could further destabilise the material, with forecasts indicating temperatures below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1 degree Celsius).In a November 20 statement, Acting Secretary of the Army directed Army Materiel Command to postpone the operation until Monday, November 23, saying the delay would take the detonation to “the latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop”. The Army subsequently moved it to Wednesday.Why is the detonation facing legal opposition?The 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals had granted environmental groups' request to put on hold a permit issued by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) that cleared the way for the operation.However, government lawyers told the appeals court that the Army could invoke emergency provisions to act without a permit, arguing that “Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay.”Environmental groups, including the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club, have challenged the Army's assessment of the risks and the alternatives considered.“The Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency,” said Earthjustice attorney Thien Chau.What are the potential health risks?An advisory warned that the blasts could release an air plume containing lead particles that may settle on the ground. “Lead is toxic to humans and animals,” it said.Residents have been advised to remain indoors, keep doors and windows closed, bring pets and livestock inside, and clean outdoor surfaces after the operation.The Army has said further details will be provided as the operation approaches.You use AI every day. articles.title: IAF has the fighter jets, but lacks the force multipliers to maximise their potential
articles.summary: As the Indian Air Force (IAF) is working to gradually increase the size of its fleet, the air arm of the armed forces is also lagging behind in the number
articles.body: As the Indian Air Force (IAF) is working to gradually increase the size of its fleet, the air arm of the armed forces is also lagging behind in the number of force-multipliers. These aircraft, as the name suggests, help increase the efficiency of the existing fleet. This can be done in different manners, such as by keeping the fighters in the air for longer by refueling them or by helping them with better situational awareness, in order to be more combat effective. The IAF's fighter fleet is backed by a comparatively small number of support aircraft. A comparison with eight other air arms from across the world shows that India has one of the weakest fighter-to-tanker and fighter-to-airborne early warning aircraft ratios.The IAF has an estimated 564 combat aircraft, but operates only six Il-78 aerial refuelling aircraft and six airborne early warning and control platforms, comprising three indigenous Netra systems and three Israeli-origin Phalcon aircraft. This translates into approximately 94 fighter aircraft for every tanker and the same ratio for every AEW&C aircraft. Its dedicated intelligence, surveillance and electronic intelligence fleet is estimated at around eight aircraft, or approximately one for every 70 fighters.The gap becomes clearer when compared with other air forces. Japan has around 344 fighters supported by 22 airborne early warning aircraft, giving it a ratio of approximately 16:1. China's People's Liberation Army Air Force has an estimated 2,000 fighters and around 55 AEW&C aircraft, translating into approximately 36:1. Pakistan, with around 410 fighters and 8 AEW&C aircraft, has a ratio of approximately 51:1. India's figure is therefore significantly worse than those of its two principal regional military competitors.The tanker position is similarly concerning, the IAF's six Il-78s support a fighter fleet of more than 560 aircraft, producing a ratio of 94:1. France, with approximately 185 fighters and 13 A330 MRTT tankers, has a ratio of around 14:1, while the UK's Royal Air Force has approximately 171 fighters and 14 Voyager tankers. Japan operates 10 tankers for a fighter fleet of around 344 aircraft. The USAF has the best fighter to tanker ratio at 3.8:1. This while Pakistan is slightly worse off than India in this situation with the fighter to transport ratio at 100:1 and for China, the figures stand at roughly 50:1.These aircraft are not merely support assets, as they contribute to combat outcomes directly, but in a non-kinetic manner. AEW&C platforms extend radar coverage, help detect and track incoming threats and coordinate fighter operations, while tankers allow aircraft to remain airborne longer, extend their operational reach and reduce dependence on vulnerable forward air bases. This as dedicated intelligence and electronic surveillance platforms provide information required for planning and executing operations.The IAF's shortfall comes as it operates 29 fighter squadrons against an authorised strength of 42.5. The force is pursuing additional Tejas aircraft and the Netra Mk2 programme to improve its capabilities. The latter is planned around six Airbus A321 aircraft, while the existing Netra fleet received full operational clearance in June 2026.However, aircraft numbers alone do not establish combat effectiveness as sensor capability, radar coverage, aircraft availability, crew strength and integration with ground-based systems all influence operational output. The comparison nevertheless highlights an important point, that building fighter numbers without expanding the supporting fleet could limit the ability to employ those aircraft effectively in a sustained, high-intensity air campaign.

articles.title: A Massachusetts father promised his son a 27-acre farmhouse, son paid over $200,000 towards it; years later, brother challenged his claim as five siblings fought over the inheritance
articles.summary: A decades-old promise over a sprawling family property in Massachusetts turned into a legal battle between two brothers after their parents died.
articles.body: A decades-old promise over a sprawling family property in Massachusetts turned into a legal battle between two brothers after their parents died. Mark Iannuccillo had lived on a 27-acre property in Amesbury since 1978, when his father, Anthony Iannuccillo Sr., allegedly assured him that the land would eventually belong to him, even though the ownership documents would remain in his parents' names. Mark contributed towards the down payment, paid his father more than $200,000 over the years and spent additional money improving the property. However, after his mother's death, the family trust provided for the property to be divided among five siblings. His brother, who became the successor trustee, sought to sell it, prompting Mark to challenge the proposed sale in court.A father's promise and a $70,000 farmhouseThe dispute centred on a 27-acre property at 94 Haverhill Road in Amesbury, Massachusetts, comprising a farmhouse, a barn and two garages. The property was purchased in 1978 for $70,000 after Mark expressed an interest in buying it, living there and operating a salvage-pool business.According to the court records, Mark found the property and approached his father about purchasing it. The two subsequently toured the land together and discussed the arrangement. His father, Anthony Sr., took charge of the purchase process and advised Mark on how to proceed.Mark contributed $7,000 towards the $10,000 down payment in April 1978. His father arranged the remaining $3,000 through Mark's older brother, Anthony, who had provided financial assistance to their parents over the years.However, when the purchase was completed on May 2, 1978, the property was registered in the names of Anthony Sr. and his wife, Loretta, as tenants by the entirety. Mark was not present at the closing because his father had told him that he did not need to attend.The arrangement was based on an understanding that the parents would hold the legal title while Mark would eventually receive ownership of the property. Mark believed his father would honour that agreement.Son paid more than $200,000 towards the propertyMark's financial contributions continued long after the purchase. From May 1978 until December 1987, he paid his father $600 every month in cash to cover the mortgage. Those payments amounted to $69,000 over 115 months, exceeding the actual monthly mortgage instalments.The financial arrangement continued even after his father refinanced the property in 1998 and obtained a new $75,000 loan. Between 1988 and 2001, Mark paid his father $10,000 annually, contributing another $130,000.In total, Mark paid approximately $200,000 to his father, excluding the additional money he spent on improvements and maintenance. His father primarily used the money from the refinancing for his own expenses, and Mark did not receive any of the loan proceeds.The property was also in considerable disrepair when the family purchased it. Mark moved there with his wife and children and undertook extensive renovation work. He restored the barn's foundation, installed new insulation, windows and floors in the farmhouse, refurbished its electrical and plumbing systems, renovated two bathrooms and installed a new furnace, radiators and lighting.Over the years, the property became known within the family as Mark's house. His parents, siblings and their families also visited it for social gatherings, used the garages for storage and jointly maintained a large garden.Family inheritance plan reignited the disputeThe situation changed after Anthony Sr. died intestate in April 2016. Under the ownership arrangement, Loretta became the sole owner of the property following her husband's death.She subsequently prepared an estate plan that included a will and a revocable trust. The original will provided Mark with a 50% share of the Amesbury property and allowed him to occupy it to the exclusion of his siblings for 365 days after her death. However, he would be responsible for the property's expenses during that period.In May 2017, Loretta signed a codicil reducing Mark's share from 50% to 44%. The trust created later that year reflected the revised arrangement.Loretta and Anthony Sr. had five children: Anthony, Mary, Mark, Elena and Christine. Under the trust's terms, the property was to be divided among them in varying proportions following Loretta's death.Loretta died in 2019, and the trust subsequently became irrevocable. Anthony, who became its successor trustee, began making arrangements to sell the property and distribute the proceeds according to the trust.Mark objected, maintaining that the property had already been promised to him under his father's 1978 agreement. He also pointed to his financial contributions and decades of work maintaining and improving the land.Brother takes dispute to court over ownershipAnthony filed a complaint in the Massachusetts Probate and Family Court seeking a declaration settling ownership of the property and requiring Mark to cooperate with its sale.Mark filed a counterclaim, arguing that the property should be placed in a constructive trust for his benefit and that ownership should be transferred to him.The trial judge ruled in Mark's favour, finding that his father had agreed to give him the property and that the arrangement created a fiduciary relationship between them. The judge concluded that Anthony Sr. had breached that duty by accepting substantial payments and contributions from his son without eventually transferring ownership as promised.The court also found that allowing the property to remain part of Loretta's estate would unjustly enrich the estate at Mark's expense. It consequently imposed a constructive trust over the property for his benefit and ordered Anthony, as trustee, to execute a deed transferring ownership to Mark. He was also directed to reimburse the trust for the property's insurance costs.Massachusetts appeals court upholds son's ownership claimAnthony challenged the decision before the Massachusetts Appeals Court, arguing that the property had legally belonged to his parents as tenants by the entirety and subsequently passed to his mother. He also maintained that transferring it to Mark would undermine Loretta's stated inheritance plans.However, the appeals court rejected these arguments and upheld the lower court's decision on August 19, 2026.The court noted that the agreement between Mark and his father had been made before the property was registered in his parents' names. It also pointed out that Loretta knew about the arrangement and that the constructive trust had originated from the 1978 agreement.The judges further observed that Mark had contributed $7,000 towards the original down payment, made payments exceeding $200,000 over the years and financed numerous improvements to the property.The court concluded that the lower court had correctly recognised the constructive trust and that the property had not been properly transferred into Loretta's revocable trust because Mark's beneficial ownership already existed.The judgment was affirmed, allowing Mark to receive ownership of the 27-acre Amesbury property despite his brother's challenge to the claim.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Michigan family used a gravel driveway across relatives' property for 35 years until construction blocked the route; an appeals court upheld a permanent easement after the neighbours failed to answer a lawsuit
articles.summary: A driveway used by a family for decades became the centre of a property dispute after neighbouring relatives blocked access during construction work.
articles.body: A driveway used by a family for decades became the centre of a property dispute after neighbouring relatives blocked access during construction work. In Michigan, a family that had used a gravel driveway across relatives' land for 35 years took the matter to court after the route was obstructed. The Michigan Court of Appeals eventually upheld a permanent easement, ruling that the neighbours had not established grounds to overturn a default judgment after failing to formally respond to the lawsuit.In a November 19, 2026, unpublished opinion available on Justia, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's decision in David Lee Shattuck v. Mark Shattuck. The appeals court found that the neighbours' participation in an earlier hearing about a preliminary injunction did not excuse their failure to answer the underlying complaint.How a 35-year driveway arrangement led to a disputeThe case involved adjoining properties owned by relatives. Mark and Michelle Shattuck owned one property, which also contained a gravel mine subject to federal regulations. David Lee Shattuck and his family owned the neighbouring parcel. According to the lawsuit, when the properties were purchased in 1987, the family began using a gravel driveway crossing Mark and Michelle's land to reach the main road. They continued using the route for approximately 35 years.Although the family had another driveway connecting its property to the road, David maintained that the alternative route was unsafe. The dispute escalated when construction work on the neighbouring property blocked the gravel driveway. David filed a lawsuit seeking recognition of property rights, including a prescriptive easement or an easement by necessity. He also requested a preliminary injunction to prevent further interference with access.Why the neighbours were held in defaultAt an initial hearing, Mark appeared without a lawyer, while Michelle did not attend. Mark disputed the claim that the family's alternative driveway was unsafe and argued that it remained usable. The trial court explained that the hearing concerned only the request for a preliminary injunction, not the underlying property claims. It denied the injunction because the available evidence was insufficient to make an informed decision. However, it directed Mark to maintain the existing situation and avoid further construction in the disputed area until the case was resolved.The court also discussed the outstanding deadline for the neighbours to file an answer to the complaint. Despite this, neither Mark nor Michelle formally responded to the lawsuit. At the plaintiff's request, the court clerk entered a default against them. David subsequently requested a default judgment. Although the neighbours appeared at the hearing and explained that they believed the case was over because the preliminary injunction had been denied, the trial court granted a permanent easement and required them to maintain it. David later died, and his son, Corey May Shattuck, was substituted as the plaintiff.Why the appeals court upheld the permanent easementAfter obtaining legal representation, Mark and Michelle asked the trial court to set aside the default judgment. They argued that Mark's participation in the earlier hearing showed that they had already defended the lawsuit. The trial court partially granted their motion because unresolved issues concerning damages remained, but refused to set aside the default on liability. The default judgment was therefore set aside, while the underlying default remained in place. Mark and Michelle then appealed.The Michigan Court of Appeals examined Michigan Court Rule 2.612(C)(1)(f), which allows relief from a judgment for another reason justifying it. The rule requires a party seeking relief to establish extraordinary circumstances and show that setting aside the judgment is necessary to achieve justice. The appeals court found that the neighbours had not met this requirement. It explained that Mark's appearance at the preliminary injunction hearing did not mean he had formally answered the underlying complaint. The judge had clearly distinguished the two proceedings and discussed the outstanding response deadline during the hearing.The court also rejected their argument that they reasonably believed the entire case had ended. The hearing transcript showed that the judge had instructed the plaintiff's lawyer to schedule further proceedings concerning the underlying lawsuit.Mark and Michelle additionally argued that the easement could expose them to obligations and potential fines under the federal Mine Safety and Health Act because their property contained a regulated gravel mine. However, the appeals court found that they had not adequately demonstrated why these potential consequences justified setting aside the judgment.Ultimately, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's decision, leaving the permanent easement in place. The ruling addressed the neighbours' request to overturn the default judgment rather than independently determining the merits of the original easement claims.You use AI every day. articles.title: Florida man sits on an 8-foot alligator after wildlife officer's capture pole fails during rescue attempt to free the reptile trapped between slippery rocks at a popular surfing spot
articles.summary: A routine outing along Florida's Treasure Coast turned into an extraordinary wildlife rescue when a 41-year-old man spotted an eight-foot alligator
articles.body: A routine outing along Florida's Treasure Coast turned into an extraordinary wildlife rescue when a 41-year-old man spotted an eight-foot alligator trapped between slippery rocks near a popular surfing spot. Justin Southerland, from Okeechobee, Florida, initially thought the reptile was dead when he noticed it wedged beneath the rocks at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park. However, he soon realised that the animal was still alive but unable to climb out. After contacting wildlife authorities, Southerland and his friend Anthony Richards joined a Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) officer in attempting to free it. When the officer's capture pole failed during the operation, Southerland resorted to an unusual move and sat on the alligator until they could secure it.Florida man discovers alligator trapped between slippery rocksThe incident took place on November 14, 2026, when Southerland, 41, and his 26-year-old friend Anthony Richards were travelling along Florida's Treasure Coast. The two had been visiting pawn shops and bait stores before stopping at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park, a popular destination for surfers.While watching a fisherman, Southerland noticed something unusual among the rocks below. An alligator was wedged between them, unable to get out because the surrounding surfaces were too slippery.Initially believing the reptile was dead, he soon realised that it was alive but struggling to escape its position."He was already trapped, he couldn't get above where he was at because everything was slick," Southerland told TCPalm.The two friends contacted the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC), and a wildlife officer subsequently arrived to assist with the rescue.Capture pole fails, forcing man to sit on alligatorThe rescue initially involved using a capture pole to control the reptile and move it away from the rocks. However, the operation became more complicated when the equipment failed to hold the alligator securely.With the animal now on a flat rock, Southerland took an extraordinary approach to prevent it from moving while the rescuers worked to secure it.He sat directly on the eight-foot alligator until the group could get its mouth secured with tape.The rescue was not entirely without incident. The reptile reportedly struck Southerland with its tail during the operation, although the men eventually managed to restrain it.Once its mouth was secured, the alligator was loaded into the wildlife officer's truck for transportation.Alligator relocated to nearby freshwater canalAfter successfully freeing the reptile, the rescue team transported it to a nearby freshwater canal and released it there.Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission spokesperson Arielle Callender explained that alligators sometimes appear on beaches while travelling between different water bodies. Their presence in coastal areas does not necessarily mean they are lost or stranded.American alligators primarily inhabit freshwater environments, including lakes, rivers, marshes and swamps. However, they can tolerate salt water for limited periods.Southerland believed the rescued animal was in a severely weakened condition and suggested that exposure to cold water might have left it close to hypothermia. He also described the reptile as appearing unusually lethargic during the rescue.Why alligators can become sluggish in colder temperaturesAmerican alligators are ectothermic reptiles, meaning they rely on external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature. Their activity levels are closely linked to surrounding temperatures.According to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, alligators are generally most active when temperatures are between 82 and 92 degrees Fahrenheit (28 and 33 degrees Celsius). They stop feeding when temperatures fall below approximately 70 degrees Fahrenheit (21 degrees Celsius) and become dormant at temperatures below 55 degrees Fahrenheit (13 degrees Celsius).During colder conditions, they may spend extended periods resting in sheltered locations or emerge to bask in sunlight.Their ability to tolerate changing environmental conditions helps them survive seasonal temperature fluctuations across Florida's wetlands and waterways.Florida's alligator population and safety precautionsFlorida is home to an estimated 1.3 million alligators, with the reptiles found in all 67 counties. They play an important ecological role by helping maintain wetland habitats and influencing the distribution of other wildlife.Despite their widespread presence, alligators are potentially dangerous wild animals. The FWC advises residents and visitors to maintain a safe distance, avoid feeding them and keep pets away from the water's edge.The agency also operates the Statewide Nuisance Alligator Program, which responds to reports of alligators considered a potential threat to people, pets or property.People who encounter a potentially dangerous alligator in the US can contact the FWC's Nuisance Alligator Hotline at 866-FWC-GATOR (866-392-4286).For Southerland and Richards, however, their stop at the popular surfing location became an unexpected encounter with one of Florida's most recognisable reptiles, ending with an unusual rescue that helped the trapped alligator return to a freshwater habitat.You use AI every day. articles.title: Boost to Atmanirbhar Bharat: India's first autonomous micro-missile system JWALA MK-1 tested at Pokhran | Watch
articles.summary: Indian defence company IG Defence has successfully test-fired its JWALA MK-1 autonomous counter-drone micro-missile system at the Pokhran firing range in
articles.body: Indian defence company IG Defence has successfully test-fired its JWALA MK-1 autonomous counter-drone micro-missile system at the Pokhran firing range in Rajasthan, demonstrating a new indigenous hard-kill option against small unmanned aerial threats. The company claims the system can engage hostile drones at distances of 2 to 5 km and at altitudes ranging from 50 metres to 5,000 metres.JWALA MK-1 is designed to detect, identify, classify and neutralise hostile unmanned aerial vehicles through an integrated engagement architecture. Its key feature is GRID, an artificial intelligence-based mission autonomy and battle management system developed by the firm. The software integrates inputs from different sensors, identifies and classifies potential targets, supports mission-level decision-making and coordinates the engagement process.According to the company, the missile uses a dual-pulse solid rocket motor and aerodynamic fin controls for propulsion and flight manoeuvrability. It is equipped with a pre-fragmented high-explosive warhead and a proximity fuse, allowing it to detonate near a target rather than depending entirely on a direct impact. The launcher is a truck-mounted, multiple-canister system integrated with 4x4 vehicles, allowing it to be deployed at different locations. Such a capability can also be useful against a drone swarm, as splinters from the pre-fragmented warhead will create a cloud of debris that will hit other drones.The system is being developed against the growing use of inexpensive drones for surveillance, reconnaissance and attacks on military installations and personnel. Conflicts in Ukraine and west Asia have demonstrated how relatively cheap unmanned aircraft can force militaries to expend expensive air defence interceptors. A dedicated micro-missile system could offer a more economical hard-kill alternative, although its actual cost per engagement and operational effectiveness have not been disclosed.Solar Defence and Aerospace and Economic Explosives are developing the Bhargavastra micro-missile system, while the Defence Research and Development Organisation is pursuing directed-energy weapons, including high-energy lasers, alongside electronic and other soft-kill technologies. These systems seek to disrupt or destroy drones through different means. The army has been using air defence guns such as the L-70 and the Zu-23, to take down drones. Air defence guns too offer an effective manner to take down drones.IG Defence is also working on KAL, a long-range one-way attack and loitering munition system, and T-SHOOL, a beam-based electronic countermeasure system. The company plans to integrate these platforms with its GRID architecture and is developing a missile and propulsion manufacturing facility spread across approximately 200 acres in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh.The Pokhran test marks a development milestone for JWALA MK-1, but the company has not disclosed details of the test's engagement conditions, the number of targets intercepted or the system's production and induction timeline. Further trials and independent assessment will be required to establish its operational performance.The army is also holding a competition in Pokhran to test jet-powered kamikaze or suicide drones. This competition is open to domestic firms only. Jet-powered kamikaze drones are extensively being used by Russia against Ukraine. Due to the higher speeds of these drones, Ukraine is finding it difficult to intercept these one-way projectiles.

articles.title: Raleigh wedding photographers who left couples without their pictures have been ordered to pay nearly $1.7 million, after the North Carolina attorney general gathered 228 complaints against them
articles.summary: A North Carolina wedding photography business has been ordered to pay more than $1.7 million after hundreds of couples complained that they had paid for
articles.body: A North Carolina wedding photography business has been ordered to pay more than $1.7 million after hundreds of couples complained that they had paid for wedding photography and videography services but never received the promised pictures and videos. According to reports by WRAL, ABC11 and WXII 12 News, a Wake County judge granted a default judgment against Holly Christina Photography and its owners following a lawsuit filed by state Attorney General Jeff Jackson. The judgment, valued at $1,713,468.88, follows months of complaints from customers who said they were left without wedding memories they had spent thousands of dollars to preserve. The case has also raised questions about whether the affected couples will actually recover their money and receive the photographs they were promised.How the complaints against the photography company beganThe company, owned by husband-and-wife team Holly Christina Scott Ayscue and Christopher Owen Ayscue, came under scrutiny after customers began reporting problems with their wedding bookings. The North Carolina Department of Justice said it had received 228 complaints since January 2026, with reported financial losses approaching $600,000.The complaints involved two groups of customers. Some couples had already held their weddings but were still waiting for their photographs and videos. Others had paid deposits for weddings that were yet to take place when the business abruptly shut down, leaving them to find alternative photographers without receiving their money back.According to the state’s case, the packages offered by the company included hundreds of edited photographs, short social media videos and longer wedding films, sometimes featuring drone footage. Several customers reportedly received only a handful of preview pictures rather than the complete galleries they had paid for.Why the court ordered the company to payThe legal action began in February 2026, when Attorney General Jeff Jackson sued the company and its owners over allegations that they had misled customers and failed to fulfil their contractual obligations. The case took another turn in May, when a judge issued a preliminary injunction freezing the defendants’ assets and directing them to hand over all outstanding edited and unedited wedding photographs and videos within 30 days. The company was also ordered to stop conducting business in North Carolina while the proceedings continued.However, according to the Attorney General’s Office, the defendants failed to comply fully with the order. They also did not provide a verified list identifying customers who had received their photographs and videos. This prompted Jackson to seek a default judgment in September. Judge Craig Croom subsequently ruled in the state’s favour, granting the judgment on October 9, 2026, according to the North Carolina Department of Justice.What happens to the money and the missing wedding photographs?The $1,713,468.88 judgment includes approximately $599,468.88 in restitution linked to 142 consumer complaints and $1.114 million in civil penalties calculated across 228 complaints. The ruling also places restrictions on the company’s owners. They are permanently prohibited from entering into photography and videography contracts, operating businesses that accept advance deposits for these services and transferring assets obtained through consumer payments.However, the financial penalty does not necessarily mean every affected couple will receive their money immediately. In a follow-up report, WRAL highlighted concerns among customers about whether the now-defunct business had enough assets to meet the judgment. One bride who had paid nearly $7,000 was still waiting for several wedding photographs, while some of the pictures she had received remained unedited.Attorney General Jackson has indicated that recovering the couples’ wedding photographs and videos remains a priority for his office, alongside pursuing the financial penalties.You use AI every day. articles.summary: KARNAL: A homebuyer who booked a two-bedroom flat in a Karnal housing project in 2015 but failed to make any further payments beyond the initial Rs 4.36
articles.body: KARNAL: A homebuyer who booked a two-bedroom flat in a Karnal housing project in 2015 but failed to make any further payments beyond the initial Rs 4.36 lakh has suffered a setback, with the district consumer disputes redressal commission dismissing her complaint against the developer.The commission observed that the complainant had deposited Rs 4,36,263 but failed to make subsequent payments in accordance with the agreed instalment schedule. It held that, in the circumstances, the developer could not be held responsible for the alleged deficiency in service.The detailed order was passed on November 16, 2026, by a bench comprising commission president Jaswant Singh and members Neeru Agarwal and Sarvjeet Kaur. The case concerned Ankita Manocha versus Aegis Value Homes Ltd.The complainant had booked a two-bedroom flat in the developer's Ananda Phase-I affordable housing project in 2015. The project was proposed to be developed in Sector 32, near Noor Mahal Hotel in Karnal.She alleged that the company had assured buyers that the project would be completed and possession handed over within 48 months. She paid Rs 4,36,263 towards the apartment.In her complaint, Manocha alleged that despite making repeated visits to the project site, she found no significant progress in construction and development work. She also claimed that the company's officials failed to provide satisfactory responses when she approached them for updates.She subsequently sought a refund of the deposited amount and served a legal notice on the company dated October 5, 2021.However, as the money was not returned, she approached the consumer commission seeking a refund with 24% annual interest, Rs 25,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.Opposing the complaint, the company submitted that the basic sale price of the flat was Rs 17,45,053. Under the agreed payment plan, the buyer was required to clear the entire amount within 36 months of the issuance of the allotment letter.The developer maintained that it had issued payment demands and reminders to the complainant in 2015 and 2016. However, she did not deposit any further amount after making the initial payment of Rs 4.36 lakh.The company further submitted that more than 90% of the construction work had been completed and that the process of obtaining an Occupation Certificate (OC) from the concerned departments was underway.It also attributed the delay partly to the Covid-19 pandemic, which had disrupted construction activities and led to the migration of labourers. The company additionally cited delayed payments by the complainant and other allottees.After examining the documents and submissions made by both sides, the commission concluded that the complainant had failed to adhere to the agreed payment schedule.It noted that she had not deposited any further amount after the initial payment of Rs 4,36,263.The commission observed that the developer had completed more than 90% of the construction work despite the complainant's failure to comply with the payment schedule. It consequently held that no deficiency in service could be attributed to the developer.Finding no merit in the complaint, the commission dismissed it. articles.title: From weapons deals to military drills, how India and US deepened defence ties in 2026
articles.summary: In a year marked by fighter jet deployments, missile agreements and joint military exercises, India and the United States have taken their defence
articles.body: In a year marked by fighter jet deployments, missile agreements and joint military exercises, India and the United States have taken their defence partnership into new territory.From American F-35 stealth fighters participating in a military exercise on Indian soil for the first time to New Delhi moving ahead with Javelin missile purchases and exploring joint production, 2026 has seen the two countries deepen military cooperation across multiple fronts.What was once largely centred on defence purchases is increasingly expanding into joint manufacturing, operational coordination and Indo-Pacific security.According to a fact sheet titled US-India Major Defense Partnership, highlights a series of developments reflecting the expansion of defence cooperation between the two countries.The document lists major defence agreements, military exercises, senior-level military visits and initiatives covering defence manufacturing, maritime security and operational coordination.The fact sheet says the partnership has delivered results across defence sales, co-production initiatives, military exercises and senior military engagements during 2026. It also highlights the growing cooperation through the Quad, describing India as a key partner in advancing shared security priorities across the Indo-Pacific.Defence deals and industrial cooperationThe India-US defence partnership in 2026 has expanded through agreements covering missile procurement, joint manufacturing and maintenance of military equipment.On August 28, India and the United States signed an agreement for the purchase of American-made Javelin anti-tank guided missile systems. Two days later, Tata Advanced Systems Limited and the Javelin Joint Venture, comprising Lockheed Martin and Raytheon, signed a memorandum of understanding to explore co-production of the missiles in India.The proposed arrangement aims to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities and deepen defence industrial cooperation between the two countries, according to the November fact sheet.Another major development came on March 27, when India's defence ministry signed a Rs 413-crore contract with Boeing India Defense Private Limited for depot-level inspection and maintenance of the Indian Navy's P-8I maritime patrol aircraft.Signed under the Buy Indian category with 100 per cent indigenous content, the agreement aims to strengthen in-country maintenance capabilities. The partnership also extended to naval ship repairs, with US Navy vessel USNS Wally Schirra arriving at Larsen & Toubro's Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai on November 20 for maintenance under the US-India Master Ship Repair Agreement.Military exercises strengthen operational cooperationThe two countries also expanded military-to-military engagement through a series of joint exercises across land, air and maritime domains in 2026.The 22nd edition of Exercise Yudh Abhyas, held from September 15 to 27 in Uttarakhand and Rajasthan, involved around 600 personnel from each side and focused on mountain warfare, counterterrorism, drone operations and joint combat capabilities.Another major highlight was Exercise Tarang Shakti, held at Jodhpur from September 26 to October 12, where the US participated with its F-35 fifth-generation stealth fighter, marking the aircraft's first participation in a military exercise on Indian soil.The two countries also conducted the fifth edition of Exercise Tiger Triumph from October 31 to November 5 in Visakhapatnam, focusing on joint humanitarian assistance, disaster relief and amphibious operations.India and the US further participated in Exercise Malabar 2026 from November 5 to 12 in Japan, alongside Australia and Japan, strengthening maritime coordination among the four Quad partners. The fact sheet also highlighted plans for Exercise Sea Dragon 2027, which is expected to expand Quad cooperation in maritime surveillance through the participation of P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft.High-level military engagements also remained a key feature of India-US defence cooperation in 2026. Several senior American military officials visited India during the year, including US Indo-Pacific Command chief Admiral Samuel Paparo, who travelled to India in February and October for discussions on regional security, military interoperability and defence technology.Other key visitors included US Army secretary Daniel P Driscoll in January, Admiral Stephen Koehler, commander of the US Pacific Fleet, in February, and under secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby in March.These exchanges brought together senior military leadership from both countries to discuss operational coordination, emerging technologies, maritime security and shared priorities in the Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: 'We stand ready': China signals push to ease business visa process for Indians amid reported curbs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: China on Monday said it was ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, amid reports
articles.body: NEW DELHI: China on Monday said it was ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, amid reports of a slowdown in visa issuance to Indian nationals."China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said in a written response to questions from news agency PTI."We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson added.The remarks come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business travellers.According to PTI, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly granted visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair provides a platform for businesses from around the world to showcase their products to Chinese consumers.Beijing has also stopped the China Visa Application Centre, a service provider, from accepting visa applications, with Chinese diplomatic missions now handling them directly amid rising demand for visas, particularly business visas.Visa arrangements between the two countries have improved since India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years. The move was part of efforts to repair bilateral ties, which came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.The resumption of tourist visas was seen as a significant step towards normalising relations after years of strained ties.As part of efforts to ease travel, the two countries also resumed direct air connectivity between several cities, including the Beijing-New Delhi route.According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has come down to around seven per cent in recent months to encourage business and tourism-related travel to India.China, meanwhile, launched the "China Online Visa Application System" for Indian applicants in December last year, allowing them to apply for visas online.Responding to a question on the status of bilateral relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi in September this year, the spokesperson said Beijing was ready to work with New Delhi to strengthen ties."The most important common understanding they (PM Modi and Xi) reached is that China and India need to be partners. Both sides are working to deliver on this important common understanding."China stands ready to work with India to improve and grow bilateral relations, support each other's development and revitalisation, and contribute to world peace and prosperity," the spokesperson said.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
