articles.title: Deepam row: Congress, BJP trade barbs as Tamil Nadu govt moves SC for review
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The political slugfest over the Thiruparankundram Deepam row intensified on Monday after the Tamil Nadu government filed a review petition
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The political slugfest over the Thiruparankundram Deepam row intensified on Monday after the Tamil Nadu government filed a review petition challenging the Supreme Court order permitting the lighting of the Deepathoon on November 24.While Congress said the Karthigai Deepam would be lit at Thiruparankundram as it had been for years, BJP and AIADMK lashed out at the state government over its decision to seek a review of the order.Speaking to news agency ANI, Congress MP Manickam Tagore said the government's intention was to protect communal harmony and goodwill in the state. He accused the RSS, Hindu Munnani and BJP, along with "the BJP's B-team like Annamalai", of trying to create communal tension."The intention of the govt is very clear: we don't want to disturb the communal harmony and goodwill in Tamil Nadu, while the RSS, Hindu Munnani, the BJP, and the BJP's B-team like Annamalai all want to create communal tension in Tamil Nadu," Tagore said."We are all standing here in Thiruparankundram. Everybody wants the Deepam to be lit in the place where it is - for many years it has been lit there. But we are very clear that in Thiruparankundram, the Deepam will be lit. Lord Muruga's Karthigai Day will be celebrated," he added.Meanwhile, AIADMK spokesperson Kovai Sathyan said there was no difference between the DMK and the TVK. He alleged that the DMK used Thiruparankundram to trigger religious debates and condemned what he described as the TVK government's attempts to appease one section of society.Tamil Nadu BJP chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy termed the review petition "nothing but the appeasement of minorities". He alleged that the TVK government was trying to retain the support of minority voters."No ordinary Muslim has ever objected to this Karthigai Deepam. Whereas political parties, particularly communal parties like Congress, Communists, DMK, and TVK, are trying to do this. I strongly condemn this. In fact, it should have been very smooth. It is a great festival, and people celebrate it with joy, so I think the govt should have facilitated it without any problems," Thirupathy said."But unfortunately, this govt is trying to create panic among the public and also between religions. So the govt itself, which is also the guardian or protector, as they say, through the HR&CE department - the Honourable Supreme Court has ordered very clearly about how to light this Deepam, and the government should have gotten prepared for it, but unfortunately, they have gone for a review," he added.BJP state secretary Vinoj P Selvam also criticised the TVK government, saying that if it could not handle "a small law and order situation", chief minister Vijay should resign and "go back to acting in movies".He suggested that Vijay undergo a six-month "internship" with Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath or Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to learn how to maintain law and order."Do not quote law and order as a reason for not lighting the lamp and hurting the sentiments of Murugan devotees across the world," Selvam said.BJP state vice president P Kanagasabapathi described the government's move as "shocking and highly condemnable". He alleged that the TVK government, like the DMK, had followed an "anti-Hindu stance" over the past six to seven months."Like the DMK, the TVK govt is also following an anti-Hindu stance throughout these 6–7 months. It's highly unfortunate that when the Supreme Court has given a judgment allowing people to light the lamp on the Deepathoon during this Karthigai Deepam day, the Tamil Nadu govt is not willing to implement it," Kanagasabapathi said."It is like insulting the beliefs of the majority population of Tamil Nadu. In fact, lighting the Deepam at Deepathoon is not just a religious function; it's our cultural tradition. It has been happening for so many years. Now the TVK govt has taken this decision. It is highly unfortunate. We condemn it," he added.What is the Thiruparankundram Deepam rowThe dispute concerns the annual lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill near the Sikandar Badhusha Dargah in Madurai. The controversy began in November 2025, when local authorities withheld permission for the hilltop ritual, citing law-and-order concerns and the site's proximity to the dargah.In December 2025, a single judge of the Madras High Court directed the temple authorities to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, observing that the pillar was situated more than 50 metres from the dargah.A division bench upheld the direction on January 6, 2026, while requiring the temple administration to coordinate the ritual with the police and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), considering the site's heritage status.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently challenged the High Court's decisions before the Supreme Court, which issued notice on the state's plea in August 2026.On November 20, a Supreme Court bench led by Justice Aravind Kumar permitted a strictly conditional, one-time lighting of the lamp on November 24. The order did not establish a legal precedent or settle the broader claims relating to ownership and customary rights. The Tamil Nadu government has since filed a review petition seeking an immediate stay on the Supreme Court's order.Tiruvannamalai gears up for Karthigai DeepamSeparately, Tiruvannamalai District Collector Vandana Garg said preparations were being reviewed for Karthigai Deepam, with around 50 lakh devotees expected to visit.She said 26 bus stands, including 25 temporary ones, had been arranged, along with free shuttle bus services. A police-manned help booth and a transport department inquiry booth have also been set up, while around 63 medical camps will operate along the Girivalam path.Garg said she was inspecting basic amenities, including toilets and RO water plants, ahead of the festival.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: NCERT warns textbook printers of blacklisting over blurred text, poor quality
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Poorly printed textbooks, blurred letters and unreadable text could cost printing agencies their contracts with National Council of Educational
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Poorly printed textbooks, blurred letters and unreadable text could cost printing agencies their contracts with National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), which has warned of penalties, cancellation of work orders and blacklisting. Acting on complaints from across the country, the council on Monday issued a stern advisory directing all empanelled presses to tighten quality checks at every stage of textbook production.The Nov 23 advisory, issued by NCERT’s Publication Division, says the council has been receiving numerous complaints about substandard printing of textbooks and other publications available in the market. It said inferior printing was affecting their overall quality and acceptability while undermining NCERT’s reputation and credibility.The warning comes amid concerns over the readability of school textbooks, particularly for Class X students. Advocate Vineet Jindal recently flagged the poor printing quality of a Class X NCERT book on social media, pointing to small, blurred and poorly printed text that made reading difficult. He also raised concerns about font size, clarity and double printing, arguing that such deficiencies could strain students’ eyes and cause headaches.NCERT said printing agencies must exercise the “highest degree of care, diligence and quality control” throughout production. The advisory specifically calls for high standards in printing, colour reproduction, registration, finishing, binding and overall workmanship.It mandates inspection and quality checks at each stage to prevent defects and ensure that only books conforming to prescribed standards are supplied. Presses must also deploy appropriate machinery, skilled workers and adequate quality-control systems while meeting delivery schedules.Any departure from technical specifications, negligence in maintaining standards or supply of substandard books would be “viewed seriously”, the council warned.If violations are established, NCERT may impose penalties, reject supplies, cancel allotted work or terminate contracts under applicable tender conditions. Agencies could also lose their empanelment and face debarment or blacklisting, effectively shutting them out of future NCERT printing assignments.The council directed all empanelled presses across India to treat the advisory as a priority and comply strictly with its instructions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Spain elections: Right-wing parties projected to win majority as Sanchez's Socialists trail in polls
articles.summary: Spain's two main right-wing parties are projected to secure a combined majority in Sunday's general election, despite a recent improvement in support for
articles.body: Spain's two main right-wing parties are projected to secure a combined majority in Sunday's general election, despite a recent improvement in support for Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's Socialists, according to opinion polls published on Monday.Most surveys put the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox above the 176 seats required for a majority in the 350-member parliament.The projections suggest that Vox could emerge as a key partner for the PP in forming the next government, potentially bringing the far right into national government for the first time since General Francisco Franco's dictatorship ended in 1975.Monday is the final day on which opinion polls can be published before a legal ban takes effect ahead of the election, Reuters reported.A daily survey by 40dB for El Pais, based on 7,500 interviews, projected 127-136 seats for the PP, with 31.8 per cent of the vote.The Socialists were close behind with 30.9 per cent and a projected 116-127 seats, while Vox was forecast to win 51-61 seats with 17.3 per cent.Other surveys gave the right-wing parties a more comfortable lead. NC Report's poll for La Razon, based on 1,000 interviews, put the PP at 130-133 seats and Vox at 64-66, giving them a combined total of at least 194 seats.The Socialists were projected to win 108-111 seats, with 27.2 per cent of the vote, up from 26.1 per cent a week earlier.An IMOP poll for El Confidencial projected 195 seats for the PP and Vox together, against 110 for the Socialists.Ipsos, in a survey for La Vanguardia, gave the PP 127 seats, the Socialists 119 and Vox 63. GAD3's poll for ABC projected 131 seats for the PP, 110 for the Socialists and 63 for Vox.The state-run Centre for Sociological Research (CIS) remained a notable outlier. Its survey, based on 8,034 interviews, put the Socialists at 34.4 per cent, ahead of the PP at 24.9 per cent and Vox at 15.6 per cent.It projected that the combined left, including far-left Frente Amplio and regional parties, could still secure a majority.Housing, corruption and rail safety dominate campaignSanchez called the snap election, originally scheduled for 2027, in an attempt to capitalise on public anger over housing affordability, after mass protests brought the issue to the forefront of national debate.The housing crisis has been fuelled by factors including a shortage of social housing, the expansion of short-term tourist rentals, property speculation by large investment funds and insufficient construction.The government has introduced measures including stronger protections against evictions and restrictions on property acquisitions by large funds. The opposition, however, accuses Sanchez of failing to address the problem during his time in office.Rail safety has also become a major campaign issue following two deadly accidents this year. A crash in the southern region of Andalusia in January killed 46 people, while another collision south of Madrid last month left 69 dead.Sanchez faced criticism over his government's handling of the rail network, with his ally and transport minister Oscar Puente resigning weeks before the election.Immigration is another key issue, with Vox making tougher policies a central part of its campaign.The party gained political ground following a surge of migrants into the Spanish North African territory of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco in late July. The arrival of tens of thousands of people triggered protests and tensions with local residents. The situation later eased as most migrants returned to Morocco.The government has also faced pressure over corruption allegations involving people close to Sanchez and senior Socialist figures. His wife, Begona Gomez, is due to stand trial over alleged embezzlement and influence peddling, while former Socialist minister Jose Luis Abalos was sentenced to 24 years in prison for corruption.Sanchez has defended his wife's innocence and denied allegations of irregular financing by his party.Vox could hold key to government formationThe PP has consistently led most opinion polls but is not projected to win an outright majority on its own. Its leader, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, has said he wants to govern without a coalition, but has left the door open to talks with Vox.The far-right party could use its projected parliamentary strength to seek concessions from the PP in coalition negotiations, a possibility that has already emerged after recent regional elections, news agency AFP reported.Sanchez, meanwhile, would need to renew alliances with smaller left-wing and regional parties to remain in power. Their declining support in several polls could make that task more difficult.The election will determine whether the PP and Vox can translate their polling advantage into a parliamentary majority or whether Sanchez can retain power with the support of smaller parties.You use AI every day. articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hit back at former prime ministers who criticised his push to revisit Britain's post-Brexit relationship with the
articles.body: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hit back at former prime ministers who criticised his push to revisit Britain's post-Brexit relationship with the European Union, accusing them of being “stuck in the past”.According to The Independent, Burnham said he would not listen to those who had left Britain with what he described as a bad Brexit deal, arguing that it had hurt economic growth, increased the cost of living and reduced opportunities for young people.His remarks came after former prime ministers, including Rishi Sunak, David Cameron, Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss and Tony Blair, questioned the move to reopen the Brexit debate."I'm not sure they're the people I'll be listening to," Burnham said, accusing his predecessors of making decisions that had left Britain facing economic difficulties.He argued that a closer relationship with the EU could help reduce business costs, lower energy bills and ease pressure on household budgets.Speaking during a visit to a Morrisons distribution centre in Sittingbourne, Kent, Burnham said British businesses continued to face additional paperwork and red tape when exporting goods to Europe.He cited the example of paperwork required for exports to Gibraltar, saying removing such requirements could help reduce costs for businesses and consumers.Burnham defends closer EU ties, cites impact on exportersBurnham argued that Britain's economy had become smaller since Brexit and that exporters were facing higher costs and additional administrative requirements when trading with European countries.He also cited the National Farmers' Union, which he said had reported a decline of around 30 per cent in exports by British food producers and farmers since Brexit.Questioning why Britain should not pursue measures that could support economic growth, Burnham said a more constructive relationship with the EU was in the national interest.He maintained that closer cooperation with Britain's largest trading market could help businesses and bring down the cost of living.Kemi Badenoch warns against adopting EU rulesConservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch criticised Burnham's approach, saying reopening the Brexit debate was the last thing Britain needed.Speaking at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) conference, Badenoch argued that Britain should focus on developing industries such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology and advanced manufacturing rather than aligning its regulations with the EU.She also warned that Burnham's proposed agreement could undermine Britain's ability to innovate, particularly in agriculture.Badenoch said British scientists and farmers had benefited from the freedom to develop new technologies after leaving the EU, including those that could improve crop productivity and resistance to disease.Taking aim at the proposed alignment with EU agricultural rules, she said Burnham risked reversing those gains and restricting Britain's ability to compete with European economies.The political disagreement comes as Burnham prepares to present his new UK-EU agreement in the House of Commons, following an agreement with European leaders on Friday. The proposed deal includes a youth mobility scheme, reduced checks on British food exports and linking the UK and EU emissions trading systems.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Legend says Lord Shiva cried when Sati died and his tear created a lake; centuries later, the sacred Katas Raj in Pakistan is a place where a centuries-old tale of love, loss and devotion comes alive
articles.summary: There is a beautiful lake in Pakistan's Punjab province which is surrounded by the rocky hills of the Salt Range.
articles.body: There is a beautiful lake in Pakistan's Punjab province which is surrounded by the rocky hills of the Salt Range. But besides being beautiful, the lake has an incredible backstory related to Shiva which is related to Hindu mythology. Welcome to Katas Raj Pond, aka Lake of Lord Shiva’s Tear. It’s considered extremely sacred. This ancient waterbody is believed to have been formed from a tear shed by Lord Shiva as he mourned the death of his wife, Sati. Today, the lake remains the centrepiece of the historic Katas Raj Temples, a centuries-old Hindu pilgrimage site in Pakistan.It makes for an intriguing destination for travellers interested in mythology, architecture and South Asian heritage.LocationThe lake is set near Choa Saidan Shah in the Chakwal district. The temple complex has several ancient legends attached to it. For travellers exploring Pakistan's historical attractions, Katas Raj is a must visit offering an experience that goes beyond conventional sightseeing.The story behind the lake of Lord Shiva's tearsAs per Hindu mythology, when Goddess Sati sacrificed herself in fire, Lord Shiva was extremely angry, sad and in immense grief. He kept roaming the Earth mourning her death with her ashes on his body. His tears fell at two places and created sacred ponds.One of these is believed to be Pushkar in Rajasthan, India, while the other is associated with Katas Raj in Pakistan. The pond is also known by names associated with its sacred character, including Amrit Kund. Its name, Katas, is linked to the Sanskrit word Kataksha, often interpreted as eyes filled with tears.Connection with MahabharataAnother legend connects the lake with the Mahabharata. It is believed that the Pandava brothers spent part of their exile here. The pond is also associated with the episode in which Yudhishthira answered the questions of a Yaksha, demonstrating his wisdom and ultimately saving his brothers.The temples surrounding the lakeThe lake is surrounded by a group of ancient temples. According to Pakistan's Department of Archaeology and Museums, the complex includes seven temples, a sacred pond, remains of a Buddhist stupa, historic havelis, samadhis and caves.These temples are believed to date largely from the early medieval period. The Satghara group, in particular, displays Kashmiri-style architecture, with features such as trefoil arches, fluted pillars, pointed roofs and decorative stonework. The official heritage inventory places the complex's relative chronology between the 7th and early 11th centuries CE.How to reach Katas Raj Temples in PakistanKatas Raj is located near Choa Saidan Shah in Chakwal district, Punjab, Pakistan. The nearest well-known town is Kallar Kahar.From Islamabad: The temple complex is approximately 140–160 km away. Travellers can take the Islamabad–Lahore M2 motorway, exit at Kallar Kahar and continue towards Choa Saidan Shah. From Islamabad International Airport, international visitors can hire a car or arrange a private transfer to reach the temples.From Lahore: The distance is approximately 250–260 km. Take the M2 motorway towards Islamabad and exit at Kallar Kahar before continuing towards the temple complex.Best time to visit Katas RajFor travellers visiting the Salt Range, the cooler months between October and March are generally more comfortable for exploring the temple complex and its surrounding landscape. Spring is also significant from a religious perspective, as Hindu pilgrims have traditionally visited the site during this period.Can Indian tourists visit Katas Raj?The current political and security situation needs careful consideration. On April 24, 2025, India's Ministry of External Affairs strongly advised Indian nationals to avoid travelling to Pakistan.For international visitors who are eligible to travel, Katas Raj offers an opportunity to explore a fascinating intersection of mythology, history and architecture. More than just a picturesque pond, it is a place where an ancient story of grief continues to shape the identity of a centuries-old pilgrimage destination.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two Michigan brothers' families fought over a gravel driveway used for 35 years after construction blocked access; an appeals court left the easement intact despite the other side saying it thought the case was over
articles.summary: A gravel driveway used for decades became the centre of a family property dispute after construction work blocked access to a route connecting one
articles.body: A gravel driveway used for decades became the centre of a family property dispute after construction work blocked access to a route connecting one household to the main road. What followed was a legal battle between two Michigan brothers' families, with one side seeking to preserve its long-standing access and the other arguing that it had believed the court proceedings were already over.In an unpublished opinion dated November 19, 2026, available on Justia, the Michigan Court of Appeals upheld the trial court's order finalising the permanent easement, rejecting the defendants' request to overturn the underlying default. The appeals court rejected arguments by Mark Shattuck and his wife, Michelle, that the default judgment should be set aside because they believed they had prevailed when a judge initially denied a request for a preliminary injunction. David later died during the proceedings, and his son, Corey May Shattuck, was substituted as the plaintiff.A driveway used since the properties were purchased in 1987The dispute involved adjoining properties purchased by the families in 1987. According to the original plaintiff, David Shattuck, he had access to a gravel driveway crossing the neighbouring property to reach the main road. He claimed that his family had used the route for approximately 35 years before construction work obstructed it. The neighbouring property, owned by Mark and Michelle Shattuck, also contained a gravel mine subject to federal regulations. Although David had another driveway leading to the main road, he argued that it was unsafe to use.After access to the gravel route was blocked, David filed a lawsuit seeking several forms of property-related relief. His claims included adverse possession, acquiescence, quiet title and interference with an easement. He also sought a declaration recognising either a prescriptive easement or an easement by necessity. He requested a preliminary injunction to prevent further interference with the disputed route while the case proceeded.Why the defendants believed the case was overAt the preliminary injunction hearing, Mark appeared without a lawyer, while Michelle did not attend. Mark disputed the claim that the alternative driveway was unsafe and argued that David could still use it. However, the trial court explained that the hearing was limited to the request for a preliminary injunction, rather than the underlying claims in the lawsuit. It also indicated that there would be another opportunity to address the complaint.The court eventually denied the preliminary injunction because there was insufficient information to make an informed decision. However, it directed Mark to maintain the existing situation and refrain from further work in the disputed area until the case was decided.At the end of the hearing, the judge said, "that will conclude the matter". Mark and Michelle later argued that they understood this statement to mean that the entire case had ended. However, the court had also discussed the fact that the defendants had not filed an answer to the complaint and that their deadline to do so had not yet expired. The judge further indicated that another hearing would be scheduled to address the underlying lawsuit.The defendants did not file an answer. At David's request, the court clerk entered a default against them for failing to plead or otherwise defend the case. The trial court subsequently entered a default judgment awarding David a permanent easement and requiring the defendants to maintain it.Appeals court rejects request to undo the defaultAfter obtaining legal representation, Mark and Michelle sought to have the default judgment set aside. They argued that Mark's appearance at the preliminary injunction hearing and his objections to the claims meant that he had already defended the lawsuit. The trial court partially granted their request because certain questions concerning damages remained unresolved. However, it refused to remove the underlying default relating to liability. As a result, the court set aside the default judgment but left the underlying default on liability in place. The court later finalised the easement arrangements without changing that decision.The Michigan Court of Appeals said it did not need to determine whether the clerk had correctly entered the default. Instead, it examined whether the defendants had established grounds for relief under Michigan Court Rule 2.612(C)(1)(f), which permits a judgment to be set aside for other reasons justifying relief. The rule requires extraordinary circumstances that make setting aside the judgment necessary to achieve justice.The appeals court found that Mark's participation in the preliminary injunction hearing did not, by itself, establish such circumstances. It also concluded that the judge's closing remarks could not reasonably be interpreted in isolation, given the discussion about the unanswered complaint and the need for further proceedings. The defendants also argued that recognising the easement could expose them to additional regulatory responsibilities and potential fines under the federal Mine Safety and Health Act. However, the court found that they had not adequately demonstrated why those possible consequences justified overturning the judgment.The Michigan Court of Appeals ultimately found no abuse of discretion by the trial court and affirmed its decision. The November 19 ruling upheld the trial court's final order concerning the easement, leaving the permanent access arrangement intact.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Distribution of cyclone relief expected to be completed by month-end: CM
articles.summary: Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi says Cyclone Akvan relief in Ganjam to finish by month-end; 80% got rice, 60% cash; compensation rates raised.
articles.body: Berhampur: Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who, along with his cabinet colleagues, visited Purushottampur and Chhatrapur blocks in cyclone-affected Ganjam district on Monday, said that distribution of the assistance was expected to be completed by month-end.Accompanied by deputy chief minister and agriculture minister K V Singhdeo, revenue minister Suresh Pujari, commerce and transport minister Bibhuti Bhusan Jena, and fisheries and animal resources minister Gokulanand Mallick, the CM inspected the condition of standing crops before reviewing the damage, restoration and progress of distribution of assistance in the wake of Cyclone Akvan. The CM also talked to the affected farmers during the inspection of the fields.During the review, Majhi took stock of the distribution of special assistance of Rs 2,500 in cash and 50 kg of rice to the affected families. While 80% of affected families have received rice, 60% have received the cash assistance, he said, directing the officials to take necessary steps to provide prompt assistance and restore damaged infrastructure quickly.“During our aerial survey and field visit, we have seen the extent of damage to standing crops. The assessment of crop damage is being carried out by the administration. After getting the damage report, we will provide compensation to the affected farmers,” the chief minister told reporters at Chhatrapur.He said they have enhanced the compensation for crop damage from Rs 8,000 to Rs 11,000 per hectare and for sand casting to Rs 23,000. The compensation for house damage has been increased from Rs 1.2 lakh to Rs 1.6 lakh.He has also asked the Ganjam administration to prepare a detailed project report, integrating Gajapati and Kandhamal districts to tackle the natural disaster in the long term. The special relief commissioner will assist with this, he said. Among others, chief secretary Anu Garg and several others attended the review meeting.During his interaction with the farmers, many demanded a special package to compensate for their crop damage.The chief minister assured them that no affected farmer would be left out of getting the assistance.He praised the teamwork of Ganjam district in managing the two cyclones and floods in less than a month, which he said set an example in the country. articles.summary: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police booked 1,782 motorists for various traffic violations during a special enforcement drive conducted in the city in a
articles.body: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police booked 1,782 motorists for various traffic violations during a special enforcement drive conducted in the city in a 24-hour period from Sunday morning to Monday morning.The violations included riding two-wheelers without helmets, not wearing seat belts, overspeeding, signal jumping, using mobile phones while driving and drunk driving.Of the 1,782 motorists booked, 121 were booked for drunk driving. Of the 121 motorists booked for drunk driving, 51 were caught by law and order police and 70 by traffic police. Another 146 motorists were booked for overspeeding, including 22 by law and order police and 124 by traffic police.The remaining 1,515 motorists were booked for other traffic violations. Police imposed a total fine of Rs 3,49,400 on the violators.S S Maheswaran, deputy commissioner of police (traffic), Coimbatore city, said 500 police personnel had been deployed at various locations across the city for the drive. articles.title: Tessa Majors was murdered in NYC during a robbry in 2019. Convict Luchiano Lewis who was 14 years old at that time quietly released from prison on parole after serving less than 7 years
articles.summary: One of the teenagers convicted in the 2019 killing of Barnard College freshman Tessa Majors has been released from prison, nearly seven years after the
articles.body: One of the teenagers convicted in the 2019 killing of Barnard College freshman Tessa Majors has been released from prison, nearly seven years after the 18-year-old was stabbed to death during a robbery in a New York City park. Luchiano Lewis, now 21, was released from Franklin Correctional Facility on October 14 under conditional supervision, according to New York State Department of Corrections and Community Supervision records. Lewis was 14 when Majors was killed in Manhattan's Morningside Park in December 2019. Lewis had been sentenced to nine years to life in prison in October 2021 after pleading guilty to second-degree murder and first-degree robbery. He has served less than seven years since the killing.According to the New York Post, Lewis qualified for automatic conditional release after serving two-thirds of his minimum sentence. He did not receive a separate parole hearing before his release.What happened to Tessa Majors?Majors was a first-year student at Barnard College, an affiliate of Columbia University, when she was attacked on December 11, 2019.Prosecutors said Lewis and two other teenagers approached her near a steep staircase in Morningside Park with the intention of stealing her iPhone. During the robbery, Majors was stabbed multiple times. Despite her injuries, she managed to reach the park entrance and climb towards the street before collapsing. She later died at a hospital.The killing shocked the Barnard and Columbia University communities and prompted an outpouring of grief across the country.During a September 2021 plea hearing, Lewis said he knew one of the other teenagers had a knife but claimed he did not know Majors had been stabbed or killed until he saw a news report the following morning.“The next morning, I heard there was a murder in the park. I looked up the story on a phone and saw a photo of the dead girl and I realized it was the girl we had robbed,” Lewis said in a statement read in court. At his sentencing, Lewis expressed remorse over his involvement in the crime. “As a human, I feel ashamed, embarrassed and sad at the role I played in destroying two families. Nothing I say or do can change that fact,” he said.Judge had cited Lewis' behaviour behind barsLewis' release has also drawn attention because of his reported history of violent incidents while in juvenile detention and awaiting trial. According to the New York Post, Lewis was involved in gang assaults, possessed weapons and attacked another prisoner while awaiting trial. At his 2021 sentencing, Manhattan Supreme Court Justice Robert Mandelbaum acknowledged Lewis' young age but said his conduct after the killing showed that the crime was not an isolated lapse. The judge imposed the maximum sentence of nine years to life.What happened to the other teenagers?Two other teenagers were involved in the attack on Majors. Rashaun Weaver, who was also 14 at the time, was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 14 years to life in prison. He remains incarcerated at Coxsackie Correctional Facility. The third teenager, Zyairr Davis, was 13 at the time and was not tried as an adult. He pleaded guilty to first-degree robbery and was initially sentenced to 18 months of detention. He was released but is now serving time for unrelated assault and murder charges.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 12 cops injured as villagers opposing coal project hold private firm staffer and driver hostage, attack rescue team in Dumka
articles.summary: 12 police injured in Dumka as villagers opposing Badalpara-Kalyanpur coal block hold private firm official and driver hostage; FIR being registered.
articles.body: Dumka: Eleven jawans and an officer of a Rapid Action Police (RAP) team were injured while attempting to rescue an official of a private company, engaged in exploration work for the Badalpara-Kalyanpur coal block in Dumka’s Shikaripara, and his driver from an irate mob late on Sunday.Over 500 people, who had gathered at a gram sabha at Badalpara-Kalyanpur village over the coal block, reportedly took Sagar Singh Meena, an official of Synergy Geotag, hostage along with his driver. The locals have been opposing the project for over a decade. The block was allotted to Haryana Power Generation Corporation Limited (HPGCL) in 2016 and has over 100 million tonnes of coal reserves, sources in the administration said.As situation spiralled out of control late in the evening, local teams from Shikaripara police station sought help. A RAP team of 45 personnel, led by its company commander Anil Das (56), was dispatched from Dumka. Das said his team came under attack soon after reaching the spot. “Over 500 people from the villages and neighbouring settlements, including women, hurled stones, attacked us with sticks, agricultural tools and bows and arrows,” Das said.Das suffered a fractured leg while 11 constables also sustained injuries. The villagers then retreated using the cover of darkness and forest cover. A few others were discharged after treatment at Shikaripara community health centre. Meena was found next to his car on Monday morning while his driver is missing.Kapil Dev Thakur, Shikaripara circle officer, on Monday said the process of registering an FIR into the incident was underway. Dumka deputy development Commissioner Aniket Sachan, accompanied by the civil surgeon, later visited Dumka Sadar Hospital and reviewed the treatment of the injured personnel.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Jupiter Wagons, Korea’s Woojin tie up to make Metro trains
articles.summary: Jupiter Wagons, Woojin form JV to make metro trains in India; Woojin supplies propulsion, TCMS, doors, bogies, shells with tech transfer under Make in India.
articles.body: Kolkata: Jupiter Wagons Ltd has entered into a joint venture with South Korea’s Woojin Industrial Systems to manufacture metro trains and propulsion systems for EMU, Vande Bharat, semi-high-speed and high-speed trains.The Kolkata-based company will hold an 80% stake in the venture, with Woojin holding the remaining 20%. Metro coaches will be manufactured in India, while Woojin will supply propulsion systems, train control and management systems (TCMS), automatic door systems, bogies and aluminium car body shells.“With Woojin, we bring proven metro, propulsion and train control technology to India on an exclusive basis, with Indian engineers building on it and Indian ownership of what we create. This joint venture takes JWL from the wheel to the propulsion system and makes us a complete rolling stock partner for India’s rail ambitions. It also adds a strong industrial chapter to the India and Korea partnership,” said Vivek Lohia, managing director of Jupiter Wagons Ltd.Jupiter Wagons currently manufactures freight wagons, bogies and couplers, as well as railway wheels, axles and wheelsets through Jupiter Tatravagonka Railwheel Factory (JTRWF), in which Italy’s Lucchini RS and SIMEST are shareholders.Lohia said Woojin would transfer technology to Jupiter Wagons. “Under Make in India, the joint venture will design, engineer, manufacture, test, commission and maintain these critical systems in India,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Ineligible beneficiaries in Centre's free ration scheme? What govt survey found
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A small proportion of ineligible beneficiaries may have been included in the Centre's free ration scheme, Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A small proportion of ineligible beneficiaries may have been included in the Centre's free ration scheme, Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), which is primarily aimed at providing food security to the poor, according to a survey conducted by the Union food ministry.The evaluation covered 51,303 beneficiary households, 4,939 government-licensed Fair Price Shops, 2,036 Vigilance Committee members and 245 godowns across rural and urban areas in all 36 states and Union territories, PTI reported."The evaluation indicates a national inclusion error of 13.2% (moderate), with substantially higher inclusion errors observed in West Bengal (39.5%), Tripura (39.2%), Tamil Nadu (38.7%), and Meghalaya (28.5%)," said the report, uploaded on the department's website.As per the report, the inclusion error rate stood at 12.5% in rural areas and 15.6% in urban areas.The report also found that Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households had a slightly lower inclusion error rate of 12.2%, compared with 13.4% among priority households.The study, however, found that beneficiaries remained largely satisfied with PMGKAY."Beneficiary satisfaction remains high, with 90.6% satisfied with FPS services and 94.9% satisfied with foodgrain quality. Nearly 99% of beneficiaries reported that foodgrains were consumed within the household, indicating strong end-use utilisation for intended food security purposes," the report added.Under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, implemented under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), the Centre provides 5 kg of free foodgrains per person per month to eligible beneficiaries in the priority households category. Antyodaya Anna Yojana households are entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month. Overall, around 80 crore people are covered under the food security law.Under the NFSA, an inclusion error occurs when households that do not meet the eligibility criteria prescribed by states continue to receive subsidised foodgrains.The Department of Food and Public Distribution commissioned the "Concurrent Evaluation and Monitoring of NFSA-PMGKAY" (2025-26)' to assess the effectiveness, inclusiveness and operational efficiency of the NFSA, 2013, and PMGKAY, as well as beneficiary experience across all states and Union territories.The study examined various aspects of implementation, including targeting efficiency, service delivery, grievance redressal, digital systems, portability, infrastructure readiness, beneficiary awareness and operational performance.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump made Putin look like ‘winner’ at summit, Haley says
articles.summary: Former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley said Sunday that President Trump made Russian President Vladimir Putin look like a “winner” during trilateral talks earlier this month with Chinese officials. “China and Russia actually don’t love each other. They just use each other to go against the U.S. because that’s the one thing…
articles.body:
Former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley said Sunday that President Trump made Russian President Vladimir Putin look like a “winner” during trilateral talks earlier this month with Chinese officials.

“China and Russia actually don’t love each other. They just use each other to go against the U.S. because that’s the one thing they have in common,” she told host Jacqui Heinrich on Fox News’s “The Sunday Briefing.”

“Look, the biggest winner of the trilateral was Putin. All he has wanted is to be seen as a global heavy hitter, and they allow that to happen by having him sit at the table. It’s unfortunate, you know,” she continued.

Haley said the talks gave Putin “stilts to make him think he’s taller and bigger and stronger,” and she called out his seat on one side of the table, which she believed made him look like “the winner at the end of the day.”

She was referring to a photo of the talks that showed Trump and Putin sitting opposite one another at a circular table while Chinese President Xi Jinping sat between the pair, facing reporters.

“I think President Xi saw that. He doesn’t see Putin as an equal, and I think he treated him that way,” the former ambassador stated. “Who was sitting at the middle of the table? Who looked like they were holding court? It’s President Xi. That’s exactly what he wanted. This was all about optics.”

The trio of world leaders commenced talks on Nov. 19 in Shenzhen, China. Trump was slated to address Russia’s war with Ukraine along with China’s involvement in the U.S. war with Iran.

After 70 minutes of closed-door conversations, the group reportedly agreed to a smaller agenda concerning U.N. reform, fossil fuel refinement and limiting the reach of the International Criminal Court, according to The Associated Press .

Putin characterized the talks as open and candid, calling the trilateral format “useful and substantive,” The Associated Press reported. He also described the talks as “a serious collaborative work” when asked if the image of the meeting mattered more than its substance.
